extracted.intended_audience: parties, their representatives (attorneys/non-attorney representatives), presiding officers, Atomic Safety and Licensing Board members, and counsel involved in NRC adjudicatory proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards governing appearance, conduct, motions, scheduling, evidence, boards, and presiding officer powers in Nuclear Regulatory Commission adjudicatory hearings (Atomic Safety and Licensing Boards and related proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of presiding officer or board member
rubrics_metrics.description: If a designated presiding officer or a designated member of an Atomic Safety and Licensing Board believes that they are disqualified to preside or to participate as a board member in the hearing, they shall withdraw by notice on the record and shall notify the Commission or the Chief Administrative Judge, as appropriate, of the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party believing a presiding officer or board member should be disqualified may move that they disqualify themselves; the motion must be supported by affidavits setting forth the alleged grounds. If not granted, the motion must be referred to the Commission, which will determine sufficiency of the grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailability of presiding officer or board member
rubrics_metrics.description: If a presiding officer or a designated member of an Atomic Safety and Licensing Board becomes unavailable during the course of a hearing, the Commission or the Chief Administrative Judge, as appropriate, will designate another presiding officer or Atomic Safety and Licensing Board member. If they become unavailable after the hearing has been concluded, then the Commission may designate another presiding officer; the Chief Administrative Judge or the Commission may designate another board member to participate in the decision; or the Commission may direct that the record be certified to it for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses interim substitutions and options when unavailability occurs after hearing conclusion (including record certification to the Commission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution motion deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If a presiding officer or a designated member of an Atomic Safety and Licensing Board is substituted for the one originally designated, any motion predicated upon the substitution must be made within five (5) days after the substitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict short deadline for motions based on substitution to preserve prompt handling of substitution-based objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of practice (conduct and decorum)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the exercise of their functions under this subpart, the Commission, the Atomic Safety and Licensing Boards, Administrative Law Judges, and Administrative Judges function in a quasi-judicial capacity. Accordingly, parties and their representatives in proceedings subject to this subpart are expected to conduct themselves with honor, dignity, and decorum as they should before a court of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs expected professional behavior of parties and counsel; basis for sanctions like reprimand or suspension for disorderly or contemptuous conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and notice of appearance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may appear on his or her own behalf or by an attorney-at-law. A partnership, corporation, or unincorporated association may be represented by a duly authorized member or officer, or by an attorney-at-law. Any person appearing in a representative capacity shall file with the Commission a written notice of appearance stating name, address, telephone, facsimile, email, the person/entity represented, and basis of eligibility or authority to represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney representation requires good standing and admission to practice before a U.S. federal court, D.C., or a state's highest court. Notice must include contact and authority details to ensure record clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand, censure, or suspension for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer, or the Commission may, if necessary for the orderly conduct of a proceeding, reprimand, censure or suspend from participation in the particular proceeding pending before it any party or representative of a party who refuses to comply with its directions, or who is disorderly, disruptive, or engages in contemptuous conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspensions of one day or less must state grounds on the record and advise right to appeal; longer suspensions must be in writing, state grounds, advise right to appeal and request stay. Suspension exceeding one day is not effective for 72 hours to allow stay requests; appeals to Commission within 25 days. If an attorney's suspension stands, state bar(s) must be notified with copies of orders and briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited appearance by non-party (oral or written statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not a party may, in the discretion of the presiding officer, be permitted to make a limited appearance by making an oral or written statement of his or her position on the issues at any session of the hearing or any prehearing conference within the limits and on the conditions fixed by the presiding officer. However, that person may not otherwise participate in the proceeding. Such statements of position shall not be considered evidence in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-party limited appearances are discretionary and cannot be used to introduce evidence; conditions set by presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing to interested persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will give notice of a hearing to any person who requests it before the issuance of the notice of hearing, and will furnish a copy of the notice of hearing to any person who requests it thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a communication bears multiple signatures, notice will be given to first signatory unless otherwise indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by States, local governments, and Federally‑recognized Indian Tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer will afford an interested State, local governmental body, and Federally‑recognized Indian Tribe that has not been admitted as a party under § 2.309, a reasonable opportunity to participate in a hearing. Participation is limited to unresolved issues and contentions, and issues raised after they become participants. Each must designate a single representative who may introduce evidence, interrogate witnesses where cross-examination by the parties is permitted, advise the Commission without taking a position, file proposed findings where permitted, and petition for review with respect to admitted contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative must identify contentions they will participate in advance of hearings; participation is limited in scope and tied to specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amicus curiae briefs by non-parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If a matter is taken up by the Commission under § 2.341 or sua sponte, a person who is not a party may, in the discretion of the Commission, be permitted to file a brief 'amicus curiae.' Such a person shall submit the amicus brief together with a motion for leave to do so which identifies the interest of the person and states the reasons why a brief is desirable. Unless the Commission provides otherwise, the brief must be filed within the time allowed to the party whose position the brief will support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion must identify interest and reasons; oral argument participation is at Commission's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of parties with substantially same interest
rubrics_metrics.description: On motion or on its own initiative, the Commission or the presiding officer may order any parties in a proceeding who have substantially the same interest that may be affected by the proceeding and who raise substantially the same questions, to consolidate their presentation of evidence, cross-examination, briefs, proposed findings of fact, conclusions of law and argument. However, it may not order any consolidation that would prejudice the rights of any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation may be for all purposes, all issues, or some issues; balance efficiency with protection of parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate hearings for proper dispatch and ends of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: On motion by the parties or upon request of the presiding officer for good cause shown, or on its own initiative, the Commission may establish separate hearings in a proceeding if it is found that the action will be conducive to the proper dispatch of its business and to the ends of justice and will be conducted in accordance with other provisions of this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows issue-specific hearings to manage complex or protracted proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of proceedings for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: On motion and for good cause shown or on its own initiative, the Commission or the presiding officers of each affected proceeding may consolidate for hearing or for other purposes two or more proceedings, or may hold joint hearings with interested States and/or other Federal agencies on matters of concurrent jurisdiction, if it is found that the action will be conducive to the proper dispatch of its business and to the ends of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to coordinate matters of concurrent jurisdiction or overlapping issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement and termination of presiding officer jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of the presiding officer designated to conduct a hearing commences when the proceeding commences (when a notice of hearing or notice of proposed action under § 2.105 is issued). If a presiding officer has not been designated, the Chief Administrative Judge has jurisdiction or, if unavailable, another administrative judge or ALJ. Jurisdiction terminates when the period for Commission directive to certify the record expires, when the Commission renders a final decision, or when the presiding officer withdraws upon considering themselves disqualified, whichever is earliest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the temporal scope of presiding officer authority and default assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer duty to conduct fair and orderly hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer has the duty to conduct a fair and impartial hearing according to law, to take appropriate action to control the prehearing and hearing process, to avoid delay and to maintain order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the basis for the broad enumerated powers in § 2.319 to accomplish these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the presiding officer (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer has all the powers necessary to conduct hearings, including: (a) administer oaths and affirmations; (b) issue subpoenas authorized by law; (c) consolidate parties and proceedings or direct common representation; (d) rule on offers of proof and receive evidence (strict rules of evidence do not apply to written submissions but presiding officer may strike irrelevant, immaterial, unreliable, duplicative or cumulative portions); (e) restrict irrelevant etc. evidence and arguments; (f) order depositions; (g) regulate course of hearing and conduct of participants; (h) dispose of procedural requests; (i) examine witnesses; (j) hold conferences for settlement, simplification, or other purposes; (k) set reasonable schedules and maintain overall schedules; (l) refer rulings to the Commission or certify questions; (m) reopen a proceeding for further evidence before initial decision; (n) appoint special assistants; (o) issue initial decisions; (p) dispose of motions by written order or oral ruling during hearing; (q) issue orders necessary to carry out duties; (r) establish schedule for briefs and oral arguments on pure issues of law; (s) take any other action consistent with the Act, this chapter, and 5 U.S.C. 551-558.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each power includes procedural limits—e.g., subpoenas require showing of general relevance and reasonable scope; presiding officer may strike irrelevant or duplicative written material; referral/certification follows § 2.323(f) standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default for failure to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party fails to file an answer or pleading within the time prescribed, to appear at a hearing or prehearing conference, to comply with any prehearing order, or to comply with any discovery order, the Commission or the presiding officer may make any orders in regard to the failure that are just, including: (a) without further notice, find the facts in accordance with the claim of the party obtaining the order, and enter the order as appropriate; or (b) proceed without further notice to take proof on the issues specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a range of remedial orders up to findings against the noncompliant party and proceeding in their absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and quorum of Atomic Safety and Licensing Boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or Chief Administrative Judge may establish one or more Atomic Safety and Licensing Boards, each comprised of three members, one qualified in the conduct of administrative proceedings and two with technical or other qualifications as appropriate. Two members constitute a quorum if one is the member qualified in the conduct of administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards are designated from the Atomic Safety and Licensing Board Panel; alternates may be designated as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and use of alternates for Boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or Chief Administrative Judge may designate alternates qualified in administrative proceedings or with technical qualifications. If a member becomes unavailable, an alternate may be constituted as a member by notification; if no alternates available, the Commission or Chief Administrative Judge may appoint a member of the Panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of board function when members are unavailable; appointment effective upon notification date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special assistants appointment and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may, in consultation with the Chief Administrative Judge, appoint personnel from the Atomic Safety and Licensing Board Panel to assist in taking evidence and preparing a suitable record. Appointment may occur at any appropriate time but must be subject to the notice and disqualification provisions in § 2.313 at the time of appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special assistants may function as technical interrogators, special masters, alternate board members, or discovery masters (see specific roles). Appointments are subject to disqualification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special assistants roles — technical interrogators
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical interrogators shall study the written testimony and sit with the presiding officer to hear presentation and, where permitted, cross-examination by the parties on issues of the interrogators' expertise; they shall take a leading role in examining the witnesses to ensure the record is as complete as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to supplement the record on complex technical matters; must adhere to notice/disqualification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special assistants roles — special masters
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon consent of all the parties, special masters may hear evidentiary presentations by the parties on specific technical matters and, upon completion, prepare a report that becomes part of the record. Special masters may rule on evidentiary issues brought before them in accordance with § 2.333. Appeals from special masters' rulings may be taken to the presiding officer. Special masters' reports are advisory only; the presiding officer retains final authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use requires party consent; reports are advisory and subject to presiding officer review; evidentiary rulings follow § 2.333 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special assistants roles — alternate board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate Atomic Safety and Licensing Board members may sit with the presiding officer, participate in evidentiary sessions on designated issues by examining witnesses, and advise the presiding officer of their conclusions through an on-the-record advisory report. The presiding officer retains final authority on the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate members provide advisory technical input but do not supplant presiding officer authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special assistants roles — discovery master
rubrics_metrics.description: A discovery master may be appointed to rule on discovery matters specified in § 2.1018(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery masters focus on discovery disputes per the referenced discovery provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal technical briefings for presiding officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may, as a matter of discretion, informally seek assistance of Panel members to brief on general technical background of complex subjects before the hearing. These briefings take place before the hearing and supplement reading and study by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These briefings are informal and not subject to the notice and disqualification procedures in § 2.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions—applicability and general timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All motions must be addressed to the Commission or other designated presiding officer. All motions, other than motions for summary disposition, must be made no later than ten (10) days after the occurrence or circumstance from which the motion arises. All written motions must be filed with the Secretary and served on all parties to the proceeding. (Section excludes § 2.309(c) late contention motions.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict ten-day filing rule for most motions; exceptions noted (e.g., § 2.309(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions—form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless made orally on-the-record, a motion must be in writing, state with particularity the grounds and the relief sought, be accompanied by any affidavits or other evidence relied on, and, as appropriate, a proposed form of order. A motion must be rejected if it does not include a certification by the attorney or representative that the movant has made a sincere effort to contact other parties and resolve the issues and that such efforts were unsuccessful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specificity, evidentiary support, proposed order, and mandatory certification of good-faith meet-and-confer efforts; failure to include certification is grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions—answers and reply limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For all written motions (other than summary disposition), within ten (10) days after service of the motion, a party may file an answer in support of or opposition to the motion, accompanied by affidavits or other evidence. The moving party has no right to reply, except as permitted by the Secretary, Assistant Secretary, or presiding officer; permission to reply is rare and only in compelling circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is one round of filings; replies are narrowly allowed where moving party could not reasonably have anticipated arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in filing and sanctions for false assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties are obligated in filings to ensure arguments and assertions are supported by appropriate and accurate references to legal authority and factual basis, including citations to the record. Failure to do so may result in sanctions, including striking matter from the record or, in extreme circumstances, dismissal of the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes professional responsibility and potential severe sanctions for misrepresentations or unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for reconsideration—leave and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for reconsideration may not be filed except upon leave of the presiding officer or the Commission, upon a showing of compelling circumstances, such as the existence of a clear and material error in a decision which could not have reasonably been anticipated that renders the decision invalid. A motion must be filed within ten (10) days of the action for which reconsideration is requested. The motion and any responses are limited to ten (10) pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High threshold (compelling circumstances/clear material error) and strict page/time limits for reconsideration motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and certification to the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in the judgment of the presiding officer, the decision raises significant and novel legal or policy issues, or prompt decision by the Commission is necessary to materially advance the orderly disposition of the proceeding, the presiding officer may promptly refer the ruling to the Commission. A party may petition the presiding officer to certify a question to the Commission for early review; presiding officer applies criteria in § 2.341(f)(1). No motion for reconsideration of the presiding officer's ruling on a petition for certification will be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows early Commission involvement for novel/significant issues; petitions for certification are governed by separate criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing motions or certification on proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered, filing a motion, a petition for certification, or certification of a question to the Commission does not stay the proceeding or extend time for any act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing does not automatically suspend deadlines or halt proceedings; stay must be separately ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to compel discovery—procedure flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file answers to motions to compel discovery in accordance with answer rules. The presiding officer may order that the answer be given orally during a telephone or other prehearing conference rather than in writing. If responses are given by telephone, the presiding officer shall issue a written order summarizing the views presented. This does not preclude the presiding officer from issuing an oral ruling effective at the time, if incorporated in the written order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural flexibility for discovery dispute resolution with record of oral responses in written orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of procedure at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer or the Commission will designate the order of procedure at a hearing. The proponent of an order will ordinarily open and close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General default on presentation order; presiding officer controls final ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the presiding officer otherwise orders, the applicant or the proponent of an order has the burden of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default allocation of burden; presiding officer may shift as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to reopen—criteria for granting
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to reopen a closed record to consider additional evidence will not be granted unless: (1) the motion is timely (though exceptionally grave issues may be considered even if untimely); (2) the motion addresses a significant safety or environmental issue; and (3) the motion demonstrates that a materially different result would be or would have been likely had the newly proffered evidence been considered initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High standard emphasizing timeliness, significance (safety/environmental), and materiality of new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to reopen—affidavits and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion must be accompanied by affidavits that set forth factual/technical bases by competent individuals or experts; evidence must meet admissibility standards. Each criterion must be separately addressed with specific explanation. When multiple allegations are involved, movant must identify each issue with particularity and specify factual/technical bases supporting that the issue meets the criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires detailed, issue-by-issue support and adherence to admissibility rules; encourages careful, expert-supported submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to reopen based on confidential informant allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion predicated in whole or in part on the allegations of a confidential informant must identify to the presiding officer the source of the allegations and must request issuance of an appropriate protective order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective order procedure must be invoked and informant source identified to the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to reopen for new contentions—§ 2.309(c) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to reopen that relates to a contention not previously in controversy among the parties must also satisfy the § 2.309(c) requirements for new or amended contentions filed after the deadline in § 2.309(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-contention reopening undergoes the same late-contention scrutiny as other § 2.309(c) filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official recording and transcript as the official record
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing will be recorded stenographically or by other means under supervision of the presiding officer. If recorded on videotape or other video medium, that video recording will be considered to constitute the record of events at the hearing until an official transcript is prepared. For each hearing, a transcript will be prepared from the recording and will be the sole official transcript of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcript prepared by official reporter; available for inspection except as limited by section 181 or Commission order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and charges for transcripts and recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of transcripts are available to parties and the public from the official reporter on payment of charges fixed therefor. Copies of video recordings of each daily session may be made available to parties and the public from the presiding officer upon payment of a charge specified by the Chief Administrative Judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard public-access procedure with cost recovery for copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript corrections procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections ordered or approved by the presiding officer must be included in the record through issuance of an order by the presiding officer or the Secretary. The order shall reflect corrections through a table, issuance of a corrected/new transcript, or other method selected by the presiding officer ensuring a clear and concise description of corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections require formal order to be part of record and ensure transparency of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public nature of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as may be requested under section 181 of the Act, all hearings will be public unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default openness of proceedings; section 181 invokes possible restrictions for national security or similar concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference necessity and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or presiding officer may, and in specified license or construction-permit proceedings must, direct parties or counsel to appear for a conference before trial. A prehearing conference in specified facility proceedings must be held within sixty (60) days after discovery has been completed or any other time specified by the Commission or presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory prehearing conferences for certain facility types; timing tied to discovery completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects that may be discussed include: (1) expediting disposition of the proceeding; (2) establishing early and continuing control to avoid protraction; (3) discouraging wasteful prehearing activities; (4) improving quality of the hearing through more thorough preparation; and (5) facilitating settlement of the proceeding or portions of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad case-management goals to be pursued during prehearing conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference matters for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: As appropriate, conferences may consider: simplification/specification of issues; necessity of amending pleadings; obtaining stipulations/admissions and authenticity of documents; appropriateness/timing of summary disposition motions including page limits; control and scheduling of discovery; identification of witnesses and documents and limitation of expert witnesses and time for direct/cross-examination; disposition of pending motions; settlement and use of special procedures; need for special procedures for complex issues; setting hearing schedule including limits on cross-examination; and other matters aiding just and orderly disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a comprehensive checklist for case-management topics to be addressed at prehearing conferences; allows tailoring to complexity and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference order and objection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall enter an order reciting actions taken at the conference, amendments allowed, agreements, and issues to be determined. Any objections to the order must be filed within five (5) days after service. Parties may not file replies unless directed. Filing objections does not stay the decision unless presiding officer orders. The presiding officer may revise the order in light of objections and may certify matters to the Commission. The order controls subsequent course of proceeding unless modified for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short objection window; order has strong preclusive effect unless modified for good cause or Commission certification occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations as evidence and procedural governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from stipulations made during a prehearing conference, parties may stipulate in writing at any stage or orally during hearing any relevant fact or the contents/authenticity of a document. These stipulations may be received in evidence. Parties may also stipulate as to procedure, and with motion of all parties, the presiding officer may recognize stipulations to govern conduct of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of stipulations to streamline proof and manage procedural aspects with presiding officer recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument before presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: When, in the opinion of the presiding officer, time permits and the nature of the proceeding and the public interest warrant, the presiding officer may allow and fix a time for oral argument. The presiding officer will impose appropriate limits of time on the argument. The transcript of the argument is part of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral argument is discretionary and time-limited; included in official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order and its contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall, as soon as practicable after consulting with the parties, enter a scheduling order establishing limits for time to file motions, conclude discovery, commence oral phase of hearing, and other actions. The scheduling order may include modifications of disclosure times under §§ 2.336 and 2.704, extent of discovery to be permitted, dates for prehearing conferences, and other appropriate matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling order is a primary case-management tool and may be adapted to circumstances; must be issued promptly after consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of model milestones in scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing the scheduling order, the presiding officer shall utilize the applicable model milestones in Appendix B to this part as a starting point and make appropriate modifications based on relevant information including number of admitted contentions, complexity, parties' considerations, NRC staff's schedule for safety/environmental evaluations, and interest in fair and expeditious resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model milestones are a baseline; presiding officer must tailor schedules to case-specific factors including NRC staff timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the scheduling order
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheduling order must have as its objectives: (1) expediting disposition; (2) establishing early and continuing control to avoid protraction; (3) discouraging wasteful prehearing activities; (4) improving the quality of the hearing through more thorough preparation; and (5) facilitating settlement or portions thereof, including use of ADR when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors prehearing conference objectives and emphasizes efficient, quality-focused case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of NRC staff schedule in scheduling order
rubrics_metrics.description: In establishing a schedule, the presiding officer shall take into consideration the NRC staff's projected schedule for completion of safety and environmental evaluations to ensure hearing schedule does not adversely impact staff's ability to complete reviews. Hearings on safety issues may commence before staff safety evaluation publication upon a finding that commencing hearings would expedite the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires coordination with NRC staff timelines, with flexibility to commence certain hearings earlier when it furthers expedition.
